newsitem.title: UK: Ldn freight - Quieter conditions prevailed end-week.
newsitem.headline: Ldn freight - Quieter conditions prevailed end-week.

text.p: Brokers reported quieter conditions in the freight market with early capers and panamaxes in the Atlantic not enjoying the stronger demand apparent for April.

Meanwhile east of Suez there was a high volume of chartering enquiry for these vessels for both March and April. As a result, the Baltic Freight Index (BFI) rose 10 points to 1475, making a total gain of 45 points for the week.
The BIFFEX futures ended 10 to 20 points up after trading a total of 196 lots. Most active March sold 97 lots and traded last at 1,520, up 10.
GRAIN - Traders report that China has sold over a million tonnes for export and that the figure might rise to 3 million.

Regarding exports from the Atlantic to the east, market talk suggested that Equator Explorer 69,000 dwt was fixed delivery U.S. Gulf early April trip South Korea or S.E. Asia at $16,000 daily or more plus an unknown bonus.

Sapphire 68,600 dwt was booked by Safmarine delivery E. coast south America end March trip Far East at $11,500 daily plus $460,000 bonus, and Oinoussian Strength 64,576 dwt was covered for loading on the Continent to China around March 20 on private terms.
Cargill booked panamax tonnage for grains from Buenos Aires and Bahia Blanca to Lisbon-Hamburg range for end March but further details were not released.
Treasure Island 22,300 dwt was thought fixed by Comet from Brazil to the Continent option Norway and Sometra booked a 28,000 dwt vessel from N. France to W. Africa.
Hanjin was said to have booked Dunaj 33,400 dwt prompt Port Klang for a trip via Brazil to the Far East at $8,000 daily.
New enquiry quoted today included Shipmair for a modern panamax delivery Plate mid-April trip Singapore/Japan range (try for five to seven months).

Others were, Glencore 50,000 wheat Tilbury/Trincomalee March 20/31, Andre 37-39,000 51' up river Plate/Poland March 20/28, Toepfer 33,000 heavy grain Mississippi/Jakarta March 29/April 7, and Nidera 20,000 57' up river Plate/Denmark for March 21/28.
MINERALS - The Pacific continued firm for capers but the Atlantic remained dull.
Bocimar was said to have fixed the newbuilding Aqua Faith 166,000 dwt delivery ex-yard Far East for seven to nine months at close to $16,000/$16,250 daily.
Reports that Anangel Splendour 161,643 dwt was fixed from Japan by Navix for an Australian round were incorrect.
Although the charterers were beleived to have taken another vessel for this business.
In the Atlantic, Elsam was reported to have covered a Richards Bay/Ensted coal stem, and Tigris 122,647 dwt was fixed privately from Rotterdam but might have failed on subjects.
Jean L D 165,133 dwt previously reported fixed by Deiulemar at $13,500 daily for a transatlantic round was now said to have been taken at $14,250 daily.
Oldendorff was working a panamax for coal from Baltimore to Japan for March/April, and Morning Cloud 66,967 dwt was linked with a steel cargo from Brazil to Los Angeles.
Period and trip chartering of panamaxes continued apace in the east.

Although, Galene 73,600 dwt was thought to have failed on subjects with Sanko delivery Japan 23 march for four to six months at $12,750 daily, there were several other completed period fixtures reported.

Forestships booked Hanjin Tacoma 70,300 dwt end March Japan for three to five months at $12,800 daily and Anangel Progress 69,406 dwt delivery Taiwan end March for six to eight months at $11,850 daily. Maratha mighty 72,870 dwt was understood fixed with prompt delivery Far East for 12 months at $11,750 daily.
Nordscout 63,990 dwt was taken for four to six months in the region of $11,000 daily.

It was suggested that National Prosperity 75,100 dwt was fixed for a trip from Tsukumi to Hong Kong and that the 1978-built Lia 69,447 dwt fixed a Pacific round for Chinese account at over $11,000 daily.
HANDY-SIZES - A number of vessels have been covered off-market on the Continent and from the U.S. Gulf and E. Coast south America resulting in a lack of reported business in the Atlantic.
Brokers say rates in the east are steady for modern tonnage.
Over-age vessels were booked by Navix with a 27,000 dwt vessel for Tsukumi to Singapore at close to $6,000/$6,250 daily and by Kansai for steels on the same route.
Tokai were said to have fixed a 28,000 dwt vessel for a Pacific round at $7,000 daily.
